promptLatex: What is the minimum number of cards that must be drawn from a standard 52-card deck to guarantee that at least 3 cards are from the same suit?
hintLatex: Treat the four suits as boxes and ask how many cards can be drawn without three in any one box.
Two cards from each of the four suits is $8$ cards with no suit holding three.
The ninth card belongs to a suit that already holds two, so that suit reaches three.
solutionLatex:
The four suits are the boxes and the cards are the pigeons.

Drawing $2$ cards from each suit gives $8$ cards with no suit holding $3$, so $8$ is not enough.

The ninth card belongs to one of the four suits, and that suit already holds $2$, so it now holds $3$.

Equivalently, $\lceil 9/4 \rceil = 3$ while $\lceil 8/4 \rceil = 2$. The minimum is $9$.
